title: Zendesk API token inside a base64-encoded Basic Authorization header
summary: The encoded credential after Basic in an Authorization header carrying a synthetic email address, the /token separator and a synthetic token, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map.
rationale: Zendesk documents that the credential string {email_address}/token:{api_token} is base64-encoded into an Authorization: Basic header, and the same composition is documented unchanged since 2022-12-03. In a Basic envelope the token exists only inside the encoded credential, so the extent is the whole encoded run, not a decoded token-only span; the email address that shares the envelope is not asserted either way. No prefix, alphabet or length is stated for the token and none is claimed. The family is deprecated and being retired in three phases through 2027-04-30, existing tokens work until then, and a retired credential still sits in configuration and scripts, so the era is not a reason to stay silent. The URL userinfo form with %2F is not authored: Zendesk documents the encoding for HTTP authentication only.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#238, Group E). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the encoded credential after the Basic scheme in an Authorization header carrying an API token credential string is treated as a credential and covered whole. Zendesk documents the Authorization: Basic header carrying the base64-encoded string (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic attribution are the project's decisions, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The API token credential is sent as Basic authentication whose username is the account email address followed by /token and whose password is the token; the string is base64-encoded into an Authorization: Basic header.
The same {email_address}/token:{api_token} Basic credential composition, base64 step, curl -u form and %2F note as the page read on 2026-10-06.
Existing API tokens continue to work until April 30, 2027, unless they become inactive first.
